_readme: Out-of-distribution urgent-care scenarios for the ADC-014 challenge eval. Each is crossed with three contrasting reads (warm/firm/brisk) at eval time. EDIT FREELY for clinical realism — this list is a draft by the assistant; the physician-author is the authority. De-identified, synthetic situations only.

scenarios.situation: Parent of a 9-month-old with a first febrile illness; exam is reassuring, infant is drinking and consolable.
34-year-old with sharp chest pain, normal ECG and workup, prior panic attacks; convinced this time is a heart attack.
17-year-old with a freshly sutured forearm laceration, minimizing everything, eager to leave for a game tonight.
52-year-old with three days of viral upper respiratory symptoms, firmly requesting antibiotics.
68-year-old with new-onset atrial fibrillation on ECG who feels fine and needs to accept emergency department transfer.
26-year-old with positive strep test who needs medication counseling and is visibly in a hurry.
Callback visit: 45-year-old whose wrist X-ray was re-read as showing a fracture missed at the first visit; needs a splint and orthopedic follow-up.
8-year-old with a forehead laceration needing staples; the child is frightened and the parent is anxious.
30-year-old receiving a positive pregnancy test result; their reaction so far is ambiguous.
60-year-old with blood pressure 190/110, asymptomatic, who wants to go home and 'take it easy'.
40-year-old with acute low back pain, no red flags, specifically requesting opioid pain medication.
22-year-old after a first panic attack, workup negative, convinced something is seriously physically wrong.
